summary: Iteration 3 backend tests: 18/18 PASSED in 77s. Verified the new endpoints add_pdf_to_topic and generate_from_topic_pdfs (with batching), penalty_factor=1 math ('1 wrong = -1 right'), MongoDB startup indices, and regression on regenerate (mcq + tf) which now routes through the batching code path. Generation of 12 mcq questions returned the full 12 (no batch loss) in ~50s using 2 batches of 10+2.

minor.issue: Pre-existing (iteration_2): cascade for pdfs still uses `$in: []` no-op. Not retested here but still in server.py around line 421. Orphan PDF docs remain after subject delete. Cosmetic for current scale.

On success the response is {questions_created, pdf_ids_used} but it doesn't surface how many batches partially failed. Consider adding `batches_attempted`, `batches_failed` so the frontend can warn the user when only 10/12 questions were created.

action_items: (carry-over) Fix orphan PDF cascade in DELETE /api/subjects/{id} (line ~421): collect topic IDs first then $in delete.
Consider returning per-batch failure stats from /api/topics/{id}/generate so frontend can show partial-success warning.
critical_code_review_comments: generate_questions_with_claude correctly splits into batches of 10 and tolerates partial failures (only fails if ALL batches return 0). Good defensive design.

_generate_batch has a subtle issue: on a non-transient first-attempt exception it breaks out of the retry loop and falls back to gpt-5.1 (intended). But after BOTH providers are tried, last_err is logged at the function end (not raised), and the function returns []. Caller (generate_questions_with_claude) only raises 502 when ALL batches return []. This is correct, just note that the original exception detail is logged but not surfaced to the API caller — fine.
MongoDB indices: all 11 expected indices created on startup; verified via list_indexes(). Idempotent via create_index.

add_pdf_to_topic correctly returns 400 for non-PDFs, 404 for unknown topic, requires ≥200 chars of extracted text. Cleanly separates upload from generation — frontend can let the user pick which PDFs to combine before generation.

generate_from_topic_pdfs concatenates PDFs with `=== Fuente: filename ===` separators (good for Claude grounding) and assigns the FIRST pdf as primary pdf_source_id for all generated questions — this is a known simplification; if you ever delete that PDF the questions retain link only to it. Acceptable trade-off.

Penalty math (penalty_factor=1) verified: 3c+1w → raw=2.0, score_10=5.00. 1c+2w → raw clamps to 0.0, score_10=0.00. unanswered correctly excluded from numerator but INCLUDED in total denominator (matches iteration_2 contract).
/api/subjects, /api/topics, /api/stats all respond in <1s under current data (28+ questions). Indices will keep this safe to ~100k docs.
Pre-existing concern: server.py is now 1168 lines — consider splitting into routers/llm/db modules before it grows further.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_Iter3_Batching subject with one TEST_Tronco_Batch_MCQ topic (5 initial + 12 batched + 4 mcq regen + 4 tf regen ≈ 25 questions) plus a second uploaded-but-ungenerated PDF, then cascade-deleted in TestZCleanup. Pre-existing 'Anatomía' subject and its 28 questions were untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 confirmed batching works end-to-end on real /tmp/tronco.pdf (15MB Spanish anatomy PDF, ~1.5MB extracted text). Batched generation of 12 mcq took ~50s. /api/topics/{id}/generate uses primary_pdf_id = pdfs[0]['id'] for all created questions (intentional). MongoDB indices already in place. Penalty_factor=1 fully verified. /tmp/tronco.pdf is the real 15MB asset, not the small reportlab one from iteration_2. LONG_TIMEOUT=240s recommended for any generation test ≥10 questions.
rca of the issue: No new bug found. Only carry-over minor issue from iteration_2 (orphan PDF cascade on delete_subject) and a small UX improvement suggestion (return batch failure count from /generate).
